name: Amisa Server
tagline: Short-lived distributed in-memory multi-model DBMS with SQL and built-in search, sold as a DBaaS (2014-16).
description: Amisa Server was the engine behind AmisaLabs, a Canadian startup that pitched one ACID, distributed, in-memory database able to act as a relational, document, graph, time-series and key-value store at once, with SQL, an integrated search engine (autocomplete, phrase and full-text search) and a file system. Its marketing described bitmap-encoded set intersections for fast multidimensional filtering, hash or range auto-sharding with rebalancing, and real-time replication, sold mainly as a hosted database-as-a-service called Amisa Cloud. The company appears to have shut down around 2016 and the domain later passed to unrelated owners. None of its claims were independently benchmarked.
statusNote: AmisaLabs and its Amisa Cloud service disappeared around 2016; the software is not available.

scale.notes: Marketed hash/range auto-sharding with rebalancing; no public evidence of large deployments.

strengths: Ambitious single-engine multi-model design combining SQL, search and graph traversal
Illustrates the mid-2010s push to replace polyglot persistence with one store
weaknesses: Company and service are gone; nothing to download or run
Marketing claims were never independently verified
No public documentation survives beyond archived web pages
useCases: Historical reference on multi-model DBaaS attempts
Market research on failed database startups
notIdealFor: Any current workload: the product no longer exists
